steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Sigh, this is my first field mission with the task force. I thought I'd witness the Chief capturing a Sinner in action.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: How did I get myself into this?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wynn, how is everything going here?

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Uh, it needs a bit more time to complete the generation of data.
Wynn fiddles with the analyzer in her hands, while complex data strings crawl over the display panel.
At the same time, the members of the MBCC's city arrest team are placing one heavy bag after another in front of you.
Not surprisingly, such a peculiar scene draws the attention of passersby in the West District.

steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: What are these government people doing here?

steps.speaker: Pedestrian B
steps.content: Looks like they're collecting garbage.

steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: So many of them, just to collect garbage? Have they gone nuts?

steps.speaker: Pedestrian B
steps.content: I don't know. Maybe some department has gone bankrupt and has come to the West District to make money.

steps.speaker: Pedestrian C
steps.content: Tsk tsk! The Scrap King of the West Side is going to face some stiff competition.

steps.speaker: Pedestrian A
steps.content: Exactly. Can't believe they've come all the way here to steal jobs...
The members of your team are well-trained. Still, the ongoing conversation around you is starting to make them feel embarrassed.
Fortunately, right at this moment, Wynn's analyzer completes the generation of data.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Chief, we've got the results!

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Let me see... Hmm, among these 517 test samples, there are 136 with M-values in the "slightly higher than normal" range and 171 with M-values in the "trace amount" range.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: The rest are... harmless?

Wynn, somewhat puzzled, takes out the instruction manual for the analyzer. After a quick flip, she finds the ranges for "slightly higher than normal" and "trace amount," which are ±5 and ±1, respectively.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Have we been played?
Wynn looks around, taking in the steel bars, steel plates, and timber that surround her. She can't help but voice her doubts.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: These contaminated materials look just like... just like, uh...
Building materials? These are the words you're looking for, right?
A familiar voice helps Wynn find the words she's looking for. You turn around and see a dark figure standing among the members of the city arrest team.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Yes, yes, just like building materials.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Then you're wrong.
With a flourish, the woman points at the pieces of cement brick, steel, and wood scattered all around her.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: These are not building materials.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: They are the pieces of Syndicate's shattered past, the ruins of its former glory...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: They are a reminder of the ravages of Mania that once plagued this piece of land, a flower that withered only yesterday...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: They are building materials.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The contamination level is very low; it doesn't pose any serious danger, but I have a feeling that all this was staged.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Like someone made them and put them here, probably to lure us here.
Your eyes never leave the "poet" who just appeared out of nowhere.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You might be right. These do look like old building materials, but that doesn't mean they can't be put to good use.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: See? The bricks are still in one piece, the wood hasn't rotted through, and the corrosion of the steel is not serious.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I can't see why we can't reuse them to build shelters that will protect some Syndicans from the elements...
Caw... Caw...
The familiar bird call interrupts Raven's speech. Clearly, it doesn't come from the black crow on her shoulder.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: What's that?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: To shelter Syndicans from the elements, isn't this their intended purpose?
Caw... Caw...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wynn, check the bag next to you.

steps.speaker: Wynn
steps.content: Sure... Will do...
Raven tries to reach out and stop her, it seems, but it's too late.
The moment Wynn opens the bag, a black—no, a gray crow, stained such a color by concrete dust, flies out.
It lands on Raven's shoulder.

steps.speaker: Gray Crow
steps.content: Caw... Caw...
Bang—
The crow caws twice and explodes, turning into a puddle of ink that stains Raven's shoulder black.
The members of the city arrest team turn in unison to look at the heavy bags of building materials they just carried over.
Sure enough, all of them are stained with suspicious ink marks, without exception.

options: It's time for us to talk, Raven.

choices.text: It's time for us to talk, Raven.

steps.content: The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
The red light from the shackles flares up. The S-Class Sinner doesn't make any move to dodge; she simply tucks a strand of hair behind her ear and says with mock regret:

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, so close. What a shame.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: If you were a bit slower, it would have been a happy ending for all of us.
Although it's not the earth-shattering battle Wynn has conjured up in her head, she gets her wish to see the Chief in action.
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's been a while since we last met. You've given us folks at the MBCC quite a task...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Do you think that Syndicate is too peaceful now, and that has made it difficult for you to strut your stuff?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Exactly.
She gives a smile, raising her eyebrows playfully.
Her shameless honesty leaves you speechless. After a while, you manage to get out a sentence:

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You know, you didn't need to pull a stunt like that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you wanted those things relocated, you could have done it without our help.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Instead, you went around defacing public property and then reported a possible contamination incident to the MBCC to get us out there. Why did you do that? To pull a fast one on us?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: No no no, you're wrong.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I had to do that. I wouldn't have been able to get you to notice this matter otherwise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You went through all that trouble, just to get my attention?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I heard you fell from a high place. Did you hurt your head or something?
The state your once-reliable former ally is in prompts you to cast a concerned glance at her.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Hahahaha...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Funny.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You're right about one thing, though. My injuries did have something to do with my trying to get your attention.
Raven makes an effort to lift her right arm, but it comes up only to the height of a standard chair's armrest.
You see, under the purple shawl, the white bandages wrapped around her upper arm. Those must be the injuries she suffered when she helped you escape.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Sorry, I didn't know it was this bad.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Haha, that's all in the past. Don't worry about it. They're not as bad as you might think. Making life a little bit difficult for me; that's all.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: My aim is not as precise as it used to be when I use my abilities, and my staying power has declined too.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: This is why I couldn't agree with you when you said, "You could have done it without our help."

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I couldn't, sadly. So, I need a reliable ally. And I want it to be you.
You look Raven in the eye. You sigh with resignation.

options: What do you want me to do?

choices.text: What do you want me to do?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I want...
Raven pauses for a moment, and then smiles, as if suddenly remembering something.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I want to build a new school over there, one that truly belongs to the children in Syndicate.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What about the people from Rustfire? You didn't ask them for help?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: That architect friend of mine did promise to help me out...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Unfortunately, he won't be able to keep that promise.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: It would be inconsiderate to make any of the remaining members of Rustfire feel bad about themselves, given their current circumstances.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Besides, they have enough on their plate right now. It wouldn't be right to ask them to drop their things and help me instead.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You're the only person I can count on now. Please, help me, for the sake of the future of the children in Syndicate...
Raven's eyes are surprisingly clear and sincere, and a bit misty, as if on the verge of tears.
Still a great actor, you think to yourself. This time, however, you consider granting her request.
Fickle as Raven is, she seems serious about building a school.
Despite the asking-for-your-help farce she put on, no serious damage has come out of it, except for wasting your time and some of the MBCC staff's.
Building a school should not prove too difficult a task for the MBCC construction team, but you have a nagging feeling that there will be trouble down the line.
You take a deep breath, ready to have a good talk with Raven.

options: I'll help you build the school.

choices.text: I'll help you build the school.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You agree to help me?
The first word has barely come out of your mouth when the Sinner before you grins from ear to ear, no longer the damsel in distress on the verge of tears.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Tell me why you're so obsessed with building a new school.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: It's simple. Children are the future of the West District. Education is essential for the rejuvenation of this land.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You're looking at her...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Yes, it's yours truly. I'll teach them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You'll need more than one teacher.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: You have no faith in me, one of the best journalists in Syndicate, a model member of Rustfire, the greatest poet in Syndicate?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Besides, when I was a member of Rustfire, I taught those homeless kids for a while. So, even though I don't have a certificate, I'm a skilled teacher—a versatile one even.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I heard the kids you taught... they all ran away when you went to Eastside.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ehh...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, I heard a lot of Sinners locked up in the MBCC escaped while you were asleep.
Noticing the unpleasant look on your face, Raven quickly changes the subject.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ah, let's stop belittling each other. We have the future of Syndicate to think about.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: As the saying goes, "If the skin is gone, so will be the hair attached to it." Without a school, there's no way of persuading Syndican adults to become teachers here, and Syndican kids to become students.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Once we've built a school, there will be a place for them to be. By then, Rustfire will have been done with their things. I'll ask Lavina and others to come over, and then we'll have a teaching staff.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: And there will be no shortage of students. We can bring the kids from the Homeless back to attend school here.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: After hearing what I just said, don't you feel that a school is all we need to bring hope back to Syndicate?
You nod, but as you do so, you realize something's missing.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Have you contacted any publisher? Have you applied for ISBNs? Do you need my help?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Well...
Raven doesn't seem to know how to face your concern for her. She simply looks away, avoiding your eyes.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What are you going to teach the kids before other teachers join you? Only poetry writing?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Give me some credit. I grad... studied in a proper university in Eastside. I did give the curriculum some thought, but at the moment, I don't have a budget for textbooks.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: While I was at the Drifter Camp, I wrote dozens of textbooks and composed hundreds of poems, but that alone took me several years. It will be difficult to write all the remaining ones from scratch...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: So, I'm planning to try a much faster method this time.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: A faster method?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Yes. I'm going to "borrow" some textbooks from Eastside and change them up a bit. And then they'll be used as our textbooks.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Your moral compass is quite flexible on such matters.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Scholars learn and borrow from each other. There is no shame in that.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: I also plan to have more illustrations added to the "borrowed" textbooks. The Syndican kids are smart, but they're not very big on words.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Once we switch to illustrated textbooks, the kids will be over the moon. Maybe I'll incorporate my masterpieces into the illustrations, so that literature can have a second life on this land...
Raven grows more excited as she explains her plan for the school, her eyes sparkling and her hands moving around.
Looking at the "poet" in front of you, you can't help but wonder, These Rustfire guys never change.
Even if there's only a glimmer of hope, they'll chase it with all their heart.

steps.speaker: Julien
steps.content: Hope is something precious. It holds a lot of power even when it's irrational.
Yes, indeed. She wants to bring hope to the children, even if that means she has to give up everything she has.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, do you have a name for the school?

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Of course, I've had it for a long time. It'll be called...

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: The Syndicate Academy!
Raven shouts out the name of the school, her "injured" right arm lifted high above her head.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Didn't you say that you were injured?
Her right arm comes back down quickly as if shocked.

steps.speaker: Raven
steps.content: Ouch, ouch, that really hurts. I was too excited just now to notice the pain...
You know without a shadow of a doubt that she can't be trusted to oversee the construction of the school alone.
